content.value: Distinguish shared class state from per-object state; implement static methods and fields without assuming a receiver.

A static field belongs to the class and is shared across its instances. An instance field belongs to each individual object. Choose according to the model: an object’s balance is individual, while the number of accounts created can be class-level. static does not mean constant; a static field can change unless reassignment is restricted by final.

A static method can access class-level members directly, but it has no `this` reference and cannot directly select an instance field. It may work with an explicit object reference if access rules allow. An instance method can access both its own state and appropriate class members.

After constructing two objects, Counter.getCreated() returns 2. Incrementing the first object changes its count from 0 to 1, while the second remains at 0. Both share the same created field, and neither increment call changes it.

Do not make every field static merely to access it from a static method; that changes the data model. A static method cannot use `this` because no receiver is associated with the call. A shared mutable field can make objects affect one another.
Predict the created count after three constructor calls and five increment calls on one object. Answer: created is 3, that object’s count is 5, and untouched instances remain at 0.
